feature1.prompt: Decorated __init__ doesn't show up in docs. The issue is that when an __init__ method is decorated (using functools.wraps), it loses its original association to its class because its __globals__ no longer contains the class reference. This results in Sphinx skipping its documentation even though the __doc__ attribute is correctly preserved. The expected behavior after the fix is that the decorated __init__ method will be properly unwrapped so that its original class context is recovered, ensuring it is included in the generated documentation.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves a bug fix in the core of the napoleon extension. You need to modify the mechanism that determines class ownership within the _skip_member function so that it correctly handles decorated methods. The fix requires using inspect.unwrap to retrieve the original method before accessing its __globals__. Ensure that the change does not break existing documentation processing for non-decorated methods.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py. Locate the _skip_member function (around the code block where the class is determined) and find the line that reads 'cls = obj.__globals__[cls_path]'. Replace that line with 'cls = inspect.unwrap(obj).__globals__[cls_path]'. Additionally, add the import 'from sphinx.util import inspect' at the top of the file if it is not already present.

feature2.prompt: Decorated __init__ doesn't show up in docs. The problem arises because a decorated __init__ method, even though it retains its __doc__ attribute via functools.wraps, is not being recognized by Sphinx due to the loss of its association with the original class context. This results in the __init__ method being omitted from the documentation when the napoleon_include_init_with_doc configuration is enabled. The solution must confirm that unwrapping the decorated method restores its proper association, allowing it to be documented as expected.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on enhancing and adding tests to validate the bug fix. Create a simple decorator in the testing utilities that wraps a function while preserving its metadata using functools.wraps. Then, add a dedicated test case that applies this decorator to a class method and verifies that the decorated __init__ (or similarly decorated method) is correctly recognized and documented. The tests should ensure that the new behavior works seamlessly with the existing test suite.
feature2.entrypoint: Files to modify: In sphinx/testing/util.py, add a new utility function named 'simple_decorator' that uses functools.wraps; and in tests/test_ext_napoleon.py, add a new test method (for example, test_class_decorated_doc) that applies the simple_decorator to a method and asserts that it is processed correctly by the documentation system.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the Sphinx napoleon extension, particularly the file sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py, as well as the Sphinx test suite in tests/test_ext_napoleon.py. They also share configuration settings like napoleon_include_init_with_doc and rely on proper handling of decorated methods.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 implements the bug fix by unwrapping decorated methods to recover the correct class reference, while Feature2 adds complementary tests and utility functions that verify the fix. Both parts must be integrated and run together to ensure that the decorated __init__ methods are documented properly without breaking existing functionality.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 and Feature2 must communicate to ensure that the unwrapping mechanism introduced in Feature1 is fully compatible with the testing approach in Feature2. They should discuss the design of the simple decorator and the test case so that the new tests effectively capture the intended behavior and any edge cases associated with decorated methods.
